Welcome to Galaxy Planters! 🚀🌱

We are passionate about space technology, data analysis, and sustainable agriculture. Our goal is to use NASA data to develop innovative solutions for smarter farming and a greener future.

We welcome creative, motivated team members with skills in programming, UI/UX design, data analysis, and agriculture.

From Space to Soil, Growing a Better Future!
summary: Galaxy Planters is an intelligent agricultural decision upport platform that uses climate data from NASA POWER and agricultural data from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) to provide personalized crop rotation recommendations. Farmers enter essential information about their farms, including soil type, soil pH, irrigation method, water availability (whether water is continuously available or limited), and their personal farming priorities. Based on these inputs and the available data, the platform suggests three suitable crop rotation plans, explains why each plan is recommended, and identifies the most appropriate seed varieties.  It also includes an AI-powered agricultural assistant that explains recommendations and answers questions about selected plans.Galaxy Planters transforms reliable scientific data into practical, personalized recommendations to support informed farming decisions and promote sustainable agriculture.

Galaxy Planters – Project Details

1. Project Overview

Galaxy Planters is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make informed decisions about crop selection and crop rotation.

Agriculture is increasingly affected by climate change, water scarcity, soil conditions, and changing environmental factors. Farmers need to consider several variables before deciding which crops to grow and how to organize them across different growing seasons.

Galaxy Planters addresses this challenge by combining NASA Earth observation data, farm-specific information, and agricultural knowledge to provide alternative crop rotation plans based on the conditions of each farm.

Our goal is to make agricultural information more accessible and help farmers make better-informed decisions.

2. The Problem We Address

Choosing suitable crops is not a simple decision. A crop that performs well in one location may not be suitable for another because of differences in temperature, rainfall, soil characteristics, and water availability.

In addition, selecting crops without considering their sequence can lead to inefficient resource use and poor agricultural planning.

Many farmers may not have easy access to tools that combine climate information, soil characteristics, irrigation conditions, and crop requirements in one place.

Galaxy Planters aims to bridge this gap through an accessible, data-driven agricultural platform.

3. How Does Galaxy Planters Work?

The platform follows a step-by-step process:

Step 1 – Farm Location Selection

Users can select their farm location using an interactive map. The platform uses the geographical coordinates to retrieve climate information for the selected area.

Step 2 – Farm Information

Users enter important farm characteristics, such as:

  • Soil type.
  • Soil pH.
  • Soil salinity.
  • Irrigation conditions.
  • Additional farm information when available.

Step 3 – Climate Data Collection

Galaxy Planters integrates NASA POWER API to retrieve climate information for the selected geographical location.

The climate data used includes:

  • Air temperature.
  • Precipitation.
  • Solar radiation.

These variables help describe the environmental conditions that may influence crop suitability.

Step 4 – Data Analysis and Crop Evaluation

The platform combines climate information with user-provided soil and irrigation data and the requirements of different crops.

The system evaluates the available information to identify suitable agricultural options and compare alternative crop rotation sequences.

Step 5 – Crop Rotation Recommendations

Instead of providing only one recommendation, Galaxy Planters generates three alternative crop rotation plans.

Each plan helps users explore different agricultural options and understand how crop selection and sequence may affect their farming decisions.

Step 6 – Agricultural Calendar

Each proposed plan includes estimated planting and harvesting periods, helping farmers understand the expected timeline of their crop rotation.

4. NASA Data Integration

NASA POWER is an important part of our project because it provides accessible environmental data for locations around the world.

We access the data through the NASA POWER API by sending the geographical coordinates of the selected farm and requesting the required climate parameters.

The API returns structured data that our platform processes and uses in its agricultural analysis.

This allows Galaxy Planters to connect global Earth observation information with local farm conditions.

NASA data is used for climate analysis, while soil and irrigation information is provided through farm inputs and other agricultural information sources.

5. Artificial Intelligence Integration

Galaxy Planters includes an AI-powered agricultural assistant.

The assistant helps users understand the recommended crop rotation plans by explaining their details and answering questions related to the selected plan.

It is designed to make agricultural information easier to understand and help users explore the reasoning behind the recommendations.

The platform combines AI assistance with data analysis and programmed agricultural evaluation rather than relying on AI-generated suggestions alone.

6. Main Features

  • Global farm location selection through an interactive map.
  • NASA POWER climate data integration.
  • Farm soil and irrigation information inputs.
  • Analysis of climate and farm conditions.
  • Three alternative crop rotation plans.
  • Estimated planting and harvesting dates.
  • Agricultural calendar for each plan.
  • AI-powered agricultural assistant.
  • A user-friendly interface designed to simplify agricultural planning.

7. Technologies and Tools Used

The project uses modern web development technologies, including:

  • HTML – for webpage structure.
  • CSS and Tailwind CSS – for interface styling.
  • JavaScript and TypeScript – for application logic and interactive functionality.
  • React – for building the user interface.
  • NASA POWER API – for retrieving climate data.
  • GitHub – for source code management and version control.
  • AI tools – to support the development process and provide the agricultural assistant functionality.

8. Expected Benefits and Impact

Galaxy Planters aims to support more informed agricultural decisions by helping farmers:

  • Compare alternative crop rotation strategies.
  • Understand how climate conditions affect crop selection.
  • Consider soil and irrigation characteristics.
  • Organize planting and harvesting periods.
  • Explore different agricultural options before making decisions.
  • Improve awareness of land and water resource management.

By making climate and agricultural information easier to access, the platform aims to contribute to more informed and sustainable farming practices.

9. Creativity and Innovation

The main innovative aspect of Galaxy Planters is the integration of several agricultural decision-making components into one platform.

Instead of focusing only on weather information or individual crop recommendations, the platform combines geographical location, NASA climate data, farm characteristics, crop requirements, alternative rotation plans, an agricultural calendar, and an AI-powered assistant.

This integrated approach helps users move from understanding their farm conditions to exploring practical crop rotation alternatives.

10. Future Development

Galaxy Planters is an evolving project, and several improvements are planned:

  • AI-powered plant disease diagnosis using uploaded plant images.
  • More comprehensive and scientifically validated crop databases.
  • Additional reliable local agricultural data sources.
  • Field testing with farmers and agricultural specialists.
  • Improved recommendation models based on real agricultural feedback.

Our long-term vision is to develop Galaxy Planters into a more comprehensive agricultural decision-support platform that can serve farmers in different geographical regions.

11. Limitations and Validation

Galaxy Planters is currently a decision-support prototype, not a system that guarantees crop yield or profit.

The quality of its recommendations depends on the availability and accuracy of climate data, farm information, and crop requirements.

Further validation through field experiments, local agricultural expertise, and comparisons with real farming outcomes is necessary before relying on its recommendations for large-scale agricultural decisions.
